The best free desktop publishing software

Brochures, zines, flyers and books need page layout: master pages, text that flows from frame to frame, and a PDF a printer accepts. Four tools do it for free, from our browser app to a full desktop suite.

We make Slop Press, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • Free for the layout features you need
  • Print readiness: CMYK, bleed, crop marks and PDF/X
  • Layout tools: master pages, threaded text, styles, and opening InDesign files
  • What you need to run it: system, install, account

1. Slop Press (ours)

Best for: Layout in the browser with no install or account: flyers, zines and business cards with a print-ready PDF.

Good

  • Master pages, threaded text frames, paragraph and character styles
  • Templates for business cards, zines and flyers; any page size
  • PDF with trim and bleed boxes, crop and bleed marks, CMYK colours and embedded font subsets
  • Works on your device and offline; open source (MIT)
  • Installs on phone, tablet and desktop from the browser
  • The AI button can lay out a flyer or a zine for you: text frames, pictures and pages, with a model on your device or your own key

Not so good

  • Still in beta
  • No tables, tab stops, footnotes, spot colours or gradients yet
  • No PDF/X, and cannot open InDesign or IDML files
  • PDF pages are placed as images; booklets are exported in reading order

Open Slop Press

2. Affinity

Best for: Professional layout, photo and design work in one app, now free for individuals, on Mac or Windows.

Good

  • Design, photo editing and page layout in one app
  • Opens IDML, PSD, AI and DWG files
  • CMYK, spot colours, preflight and bleed
  • Master pages, linked text frames, paragraph and character styles; works offline after activation

Not so good

  • Needs a free Canva account and a connection to download and activate
  • Canva AI tools inside it need a paid Canva plan
  • No Linux version; iPad still being built

Affinity website · Sources: Affinity home, Affinity download and FAQ, Affinity print design guide, Affinity help: master pages, Affinity help: linking text frames, Affinity help: templates, Affinity additional terms

3. Scribus

Best for: A free, open source layout program on any desktop, Linux included, with PDF/X and colour management.

Good

  • Open source, on Linux, BSD, macOS and Windows
  • Colour separations, CMYK, spot colours and ICC colour management
  • PDF/X export for print
  • IDML import in version 1.6

Not so good

  • A desktop install
  • No collaboration features in its manual

Scribus website · Sources: Scribus on SourceForge, Scribus releases, Scribus manual: PDF/X-3, Scribus 1.6 new features, Scribus manual: master pages, Scribus manual: text frames, Scribus manual: styles, Scribus manual: PDF options, Scribus manual: shortcuts

4. Canva

Best for: Quick, template-based designs in a browser, for people who do not need professional layout tools.

Good

  • Over 1.6 million templates and 4.7 million photos, videos, graphics and audio
  • PDF, JPG and PNG export on the free plan
  • PDF Print download with a crop marks and bleed option
  • Up to 20 AI uses on the free plan

Not so good

  • CMYK export for print is a Pro feature
  • Text does not flow from one text box to the next; its help does not mention master pages or IDML import

Canva website · Sources: Canva home, Canva pricing, Canva help: margins, bleed and crop marks, Canva help: text across text boxes, Canva help: Brand Kit text styles, Canva help: CMYK for print, Canva desktop apps, Canva beginners guide, Canva terms of use

Which one to choose

Slop Press is our pick for flyers, zines and business cards: master pages, threaded text and styles in a browser, with no account, a CMYK PDF with bleed and crop marks, and it installs from the browser and works offline. It is in beta and lacks PDF/X, tables and spot colours.

Choose Affinity if you need professional print features such as PDF/X, spot colours and IDML import, are on Mac or Windows and accept a Canva account. Choose Scribus for a free, open source desktop program on any system, Linux included. Choose Canva for quick template designs; it keeps CMYK export for Pro.

Questions

Is there a free alternative to InDesign?

Yes. Slop Press has InDesign-style tools in a browser, with no account, but cannot open InDesign files. If you need to open IDML files or export PDF/X, Affinity (free for individuals) and Scribus do both.

Which free layout software exports CMYK for print?

Affinity, Scribus and Slop Press write CMYK colours for free. Canva keeps CMYK export for its Pro plan.

Can I do page layout in a browser?

Slop Press and Canva run in a browser; Canva also has Windows and Mac apps. Affinity and Scribus are desktop programs.

Do I need an account?

Affinity and Canva need a Canva account; Affinity needs it to download and activate. Slop Press needs no account.
